20ncb.name: 20th Naval Construction Battalion
20ncb.note: Seabees. Formed at the Naval Construction Training Center, Norfolk, August 1942. Sailed in two waves, from San Francisco on 6 Oct and from San Pedro on 29 Nov 1942 (ncbhist-020/p10-p11), and reunited at Nouméa on 13 Dec 1942. In May-June 1943 it split: a Forward Echelon of about 500 men (the 1st Section) went to Townsville, Woodlark and Kiriwina with the Seventh Fleet; the Rear Echelon (the 2nd Section; its rolls are headed "Detachment" in Sep 1943 and "Second Section" from Dec 1943) went by Guadalcanal and the Russells to New Georgia with the Third Fleet. Reunited on Banika, Russell Islands, 6 Jun 1944; home in September 1944; Saipan and Okinawa in 1945 (in two echelons, April and May); broken up there on 29 Aug 1945, its men transferred to the 15th, 36th, 79th and 126th Battalions (ncbhist-020/p2-p3; rg24-190273312/p0835). Its 1942 rolls number the sections the other way round: the roll headed "Sec 2" in Oct 1942 is the first wave, forwarded from Nouméa, while "Section 1" was still at Port Hueneme.

79ncb.name: 79th Naval Construction Battalion
79ncb.note: Seabees. Formed at Norfolk; Gulfport and Port Hueneme, then Alaska (Kodiak, Amchitka and Cold Bay), May 1943 - September 1944; Camp Parks; Saipan and Okinawa, 1945, in the 11th Construction Brigade (ncbhist-079/p2-p3). Only its 1945 is transcribed here.

Norfolk.note: Naval Station Norfolk (the Naval Operating Base), where the Naval Construction Training Center was.

Guadalcanal.note: Kukum, by Lunga Point, Guadalcanal (OSM Nominatim: Kukum, Honiara): the base area. Stands for the island when the record names only the island.

Russell Islands.note: Mbanika (Banika), Russell Islands (OSM Nominatim): stands for the group when the record names only the Russells.

Banika.note: Yandina, on Banika (Mbanika) Island, Russell Islands; Banika itself isn't in OSM under that name.

Woodlark.note: Guasopa, at the east end of Woodlark Island, where the base and airfield were. matched: Guasopa, Samarai-Murua District, Milne Bay, Papua New Guinea

Oloana Bay.note: Oloana Bay, on Vangunu's south shore in Wickham Anchorage (the card's "Ohene Bay" and "Oleana Bay"). matched: Oloana Bay, Western, Solomon Islands

Kiriwina.note: matched: Losuia, Kiriwina-Goodenough District, Milne Bay, Southern Region, Papua New Guinea

Bau Island.note: In Rendova Harbor, off the north end of Rendova Island.

Ondonga.note: Not in OpenStreetMap. Ondonga lies on the peninsula between Diamond Narrows (south) and Hathorn Sound (north) at the west end of New Georgia (Pacific Wrecks, Ondonga Airfield): placed between OSM's Diamond Narrows (-8.2677, 157.1946) and Hathorn Sound (-8.2167, 157.1930), on the New Georgia side. Good to a few km.

Milne Bay.note: matched: Alotau, Milne Bay District, Alotau District, Milne Bay, Southern Region, Papua New Guinea

Camp Parks.note: Camp Parks, near Shoemaker (now Dublin), California.

Saipan.note: matched: Saipan, Garapan, Saipan Municipality, Northern Mariana Islands, 96950, United States

Chimu Wan.note: Placed at Kin, on Chimu Wan (Kin Bay), Okinawa. Kept (audit 30 Oct 2026): the bay, not the quarter of Kin that OSM offers 1.5 km north.

Okinawa.note: Near Okinawa City, in the middle of the island: stands for Okinawa when the record doesn't say where on it.

Koli Point.note: Koli Point, Guadalcanal: not in OpenStreetMap. On the north coast about 15 miles east of Henderson Field (Pacific Wrecks, Koli Airfield); placed between OSM's Honiara International Airport (-9.4294, 160.0499) and Tetere (-9.4415, 160.2193), on the shore. Good to about 5 km.

Renard Sound.note: matched: Renard Sound, Yandina, Central Province, Solomon Islands

Roviana.note: Roviana Lagoon, New Georgia (OSM's centre of the lagoon). Stands for the chronology's "East Rovianna", which isn't placed more closely.

Gushikawa.note: matched: Gushikawa, Uruma, Okinawa Prefecture, Japan. The card's "Gusikawa".

Awase.note: matched: Awase, Okinawa, Okinawa Prefecture, Japan. The card's "Awashi Airstrip" (Awase airfield).

San Francisco.note: matched: San Francisco, California, United States

San Pedro.note: matched: San Pedro, Los Angeles, California

rows.station: Rec'd 20 Aug 42 From: NCTC-NOB NORVA
rows.note: The battalion's first Report of Changes: its men received from the Naval Construction Training Center, Naval Operating Base, Norfolk, Va. (NORVA). Every man on the 1942 rolls has "20 Aug 42" as the date first received on board.

rows.station: 20th CB left Norfolk 14 Sep'42 for Hueneme.
rows.note: The log cites CO Norfolk's letter of 12 Sep 1942. Across the country by train, presumably.

rows.station: ABD - Hueneme ... Ready Date - 28 Sep'42
rows.note: The Advance Base Depot, Port Hueneme, Calif. When the battalion arrived there isn't given; the date is its "ready date".

rows.station: Departed U.S. ... 10/6/42
rows.note: The chronology: "Left United States, San Francisco, California. 12 Officers, 591 Enlisted Men. Lieutenant Dudley in Charge" (ncbhist-020/p10). The early history (enclosure H of the officer in charge's letter of 31 May 1944) quoted on the card. The card's own header has "Left ABD - 1st Wave, 15 Oct'42" struck out and "6 Oct'42" typed beside it; its log calls 15 Oct approximate: the first wave "left Hueneme on rush call for temporary stevedoring assignment."

rows.station: Arrived Noumea ... 10/20/42
rows.note: Building the Navy's Bases: "600 men of the 20th Construction Battalion arrived in Noumea on October 21, 1942 ... stevedoring activities." (bases-24).

rows.station: From Advance Base Depot Port Hueneme, Calif.
rows.note: The roll headed "Section 1" for September 1942, forwarded 28 Oct 1942: this half was still at Port Hueneme.

rows.station: From 20th U.S.N.Const. Batt. Sect.#2, White Poppy, c/o Postmaster, San Francisco, Calif.
rows.note: The roll headed "Sec 2" for the quarter ending 31 Oct 1942, forwarded 9 Nov 1942. White Poppy was Nouméa's code name. The rolls' "Section 2" is this first wave.

rows.station: 2nd Wave departed and Batt. will resume operation as a unit
rows.note: "Roster for 2nd Wave shows 9 officers and 401 men."

rows.station: Left united States, Port Hueneme, California. (San Pedro, California). 11 Officers, 403 Enlisted Men.
rows.note: The narrative: "The second section, with Commander Jones in charge, left San Pedro, California, on November 29th" (ncbhist-020/p7). The card logs the second wave's departure on 26 November (ncbhist-020/p2).

rows.station: Sections 1 and 2 united 13 Dec'42.
20th C.B. at White Poppy engaged in stevedore work and upon relief by 2nd CB Special will engage construction projects in White Poppy area.
rows.note: The log entry's date.

rows.station: At Noumea. One-half of this batt to be detached at early date.
rows.note: From ComNavBasesSoPac's letter to ComSoPac of 11 May 1943.

rows.station: Departed Noumea ... 5/13/43
rows.note: About half the battalion (18 officers), transferred to ALDER and "known as Forward Echelon" (1 Jun 1943 report); from October 1943 the 1st Section.

rows.station: Arrived Townsville, Australia ... 5/20/43
Rec 23 May 43 From BCDD, Noumea
rows.note: Many men received from the Base Construction Depot Detachment, Nouméa, into the half that stayed ("balance of batt remaining at Epic", ncbhist-020/p2).

rows.station: Underway from NOUMEA, NEW CALEDONIA for GUADALCANAL in accordance with Commander Task Force 32 Movement Order A7-43.
rows.note: Transport Division Two (Task Unit 32.8.2) sailed at 1500 local time: PRESIDENT JACKSON (flagship), PRESIDENT HAYES, PRESIDENT ADAMS, McCAWLEY and LA SALLE, loaded at Nouméa in late May with the 20th and other units (rg38-134266079/p0015). The Seabee Museum's chronology dates the Rear Echelon's second echelon (14 officers, 500 men) from Nouméa on 8 June; its first echelon (1 officer, 50 men) left on 29 May and reached Guadalcanal on 2 June, ship not recorded (ncbhist-020/p11).

rows.station: McCAWLEY completed unloading troops and material of 70th Coast Artillery Unit, Naval Base personnel unit, 20th Naval Construction Battalion.
rows.note: Transport Division Two's war diary: anchored off Koli Point, Guadalcanal, at 1015 on 11 June; PRESIDENT ADAMS also unloaded men and material of the 20th that evening. The chronology has the second echelon arrive on 11 June and join the first; the Bureau's card has "arrived Guadalcanal 14 Jun'43" (ncbhist-020/p2).

rows.station: Arrived Banika, Russell Islands.
rows.note: The chronology: left Guadalcanal 12 June (15 officers, 550 men), arrived Banika 13 June. On 12 June LST-354 and LCTs 62 and 133 delivered 1,100 tons of the 20th's equipment to North Renard, Russell Islands (CTG 32.3 war diary); the 20th's bivouac was the north side of Renard Sound (rg38-134297927/p0096). The card has "Russell Is. 16 Jun'43" (ncbhist-020/p2). Drawn at Renard Sound.

rows.station: Departed Townsville ... 6/26/43
Group One left Russell islands for Vanagunu, New Georgia. ... Group Two left Russell Islands for viru, New Georgia.
rows.note: Loaded at Wernham Cove and the north side of Renard Sound on D-1 day (the Eastern Force loading order): see voyages.csv. A third group (1 officer, 5 men) went back to Guadalcanal with the battalion's records, kept at Koli Point until 27 August.

links.label: COMTASKFOR 31 war diary, 6/17-30/43 (Enc - Operation Orders), page 283

rows.station: The entire convoy hove to at 0335 on 30 June some two miles off Oloana Bay in Wickham Anchorage.
rows.note: Marines in the Central Solomons: Colonel Brown's force for Vangunu was his 2nd Battalion, 103d Infantry, a battery of the 70th Coast Artillery "and half of the 20th NCB". The battalion's card: "Echelon split into 2 groups; 1 1/2 companies under Lt. Riordan going to Ohene Bay, Vangunu Is.; 1 Company under Lt. Sanders going to Viru Harbor, New Georgia Is." (ncbhist-020/p2).

rows.station: Arrived Woodlark Is. ... 6/30/43
rows.note: With the landing on Woodlark: "a naval base unit to which about 500 men of the 20th Construction Battalion were attached" (bases-26).

rows.station: At the third of those June 30th landings, the one at Viru Harbor, the first echelon of the 20th Seabees accompanied the landing ... On July 2, they returned and landed
rows.note: To build a base for PT boats. Marines in the Central Solomons puts "one-half of Company D, 20th Naval Construction Battalion" in the Viru force (mcsol ch. 2); the card, one company under Lt. Sanders (ncbhist-020/p2). Building the Navy's Bases has a second echelon land on 1 July and a third on 3 July.

rows.station: 12 officers and 402 men at Oleana Bay.
rows.note: The 1 Aug 1943 report.

rows.station: Detachment of 2 officers, 1 warrant and 142 men are at Viru Harbor under Lt. W. L. Sanders.
rows.note: The 1 Aug 1943 report. The August report gives the Viru detachment as 3 officers and 128 men (ncbhist-020/p3).

rows.station: Third Echelon. Two officers, 94 Enlisted men. Left Viru for East Rovianna. ... Third Echelon arrived East Rovianna.
rows.note: Group Two (the Viru company) left Viru Harbor in echelons on 5, 6 and 9 September 1943 for East Rovianna and Doke Doke; the group at East Rovianna also worked at Munda. Drawn at Roviana Lagoon.

rows.station: Group One, First Echelon arrived Bau Island.
rows.note: Group One's First Echelon (3 officers, 114 men) left Vangunu on 9 September. Commander Task Group 31.3's war diary of 8 September orders APc 37 and APc 42 to take LCTs 145 and 146, "loading one-half company of 20th Construction Battalion" at Oliana, to Munda. The PT-boat base on Bau Island was in Rendova Harbor, across from Munda.

rows.station: In September 1943, at the request of the 6th Army, 12 officers and 306 men of the 20th Battalion were sent to Kiriwina
rows.note: To help build the airfields; the rest stayed on Woodlark. Day of the month assumed. The card has the same numbers from the 1 Sep 1943 report (ncbhist-020/p2).

rows.station: Naval Construction Battalion #20 Detachment
rows.note: The Rear Echelon's own roll for the quarter ending 30 Sep 1943 (549 men brought forward, recapitulation p0344), forwarded from Navy 250 on 3 Nov 1943 (p0306). No position: its two groups were at Viru Harbor and Oloana Bay.

rows.station: A detachment of 3 officers and 114 men departed for Base Is. for duty.
rows.note: The 1 Oct 1943 report. "Base Is." is taken to be Bau Island, where the battalion built a PT-boat base from October (bases-25); Pacific Wrecks has the Seabees there come from Viru Harbor.

rows.station: On Bau Island, beginning in october 1943, a PT-boat base was built by the 20th Battalion.
rows.note: In Rendova Harbor. Day of the month assumed. In the same months the battalion built the boat pool on Doke Doke Island and, in October-November, LCT landings at Ondonga (bases-25).

links.label: Pacific Wrecks: Bau Island PT base

rows.station: Group One, Second Echelon left Vangunu for Ondonga, New Georgia.
rows.note: 10 officers and 262 men, on 9 and 15 October 1943.

rows.station: 20th CB, 2nd Sect., operating at Wickham, Ondonga, Bau Is., Roviana, Doke-Koke Is.
rows.note: The 1 Nov 1943 report. The section was spread over all five; drawn at Ondonga, where its headquarters was by December (its first echelon left from there for the Russells on 31 Dec).

rows.station: From 20th U.S.N. Const. Batt. Detachment Navy 250
rows.note: The forwarding sheet of the 30 Sep 1943 roll, signed by Lt. Comdr. J. T. Riordan, Officer in Charge. Navy 250 is Munda, New Georgia (Navy Numbers list): the section's mail address, not necessarily a camp. Its sick went to the Naval Base Hospital, Navy 250, through December.

rows.station: Group Two, first and Second Echelons left East Rovianna and arrived at Bau Island on 5 November 1943.
rows.note: Left East Rovianna 25 October - 5 November.

rows.station: 20th CB, Sect. 1 located at Kiriwina, to move to Woodlark in December.
rows.note: From a November 1943 Seventh Fleet letter. When the Kiriwina detachment rejoined isn't given; drawn at Woodlark from the end of December.

rows.station: 31 Dec'43, first echelon of 3 officers and 54 men departed from Ondonga for the Russells. Unit at Bau consists of 4 officers and 195 men. Unit at Doke-Koke consists of 1 officer and 15 men.
rows.note: The 1 Jan 1944 report: the section was detached from the 15th Regiment on 20 Dec 1943 and ordered to the Russells to operate the ABCD annex; work at Bau "continued ... awaiting transportation".

rows.station: All personnel, Four Officers and 211 Enlisted Men, left Bau Island and sailed for Russell Islands.
rows.note: The ship isn't named.

rows.station: All personnel of section Two Arrived at Banika, Russell Islands and are united. Total 14 Officers, 467 Enlisted Men.
rows.note: The Ondonga group came in two parties (1 officer and 54 men, 1-2 January; 9 officers and 202 men, 9-10 January); on 28 December 1943 APc 45 and LCT 367 were on their way to Ondonga to load the 20th for the Russells (CTG 31.3 war diary).

rows.station: This batt. reported at Russell Is. on 1 Jan and 13 Jan'44.
rows.note: "In January 1944, the second section of the 20th Battalion arrived to operate the ABCD annex" (bases-25): the advance base construction depot annex on Banika, receiving and shipping material, assembling vehicles, servicing cranes and bulldozers.

rows.station: Work was completed at Woodlark 16 Apr'44. Embarked 16 Apr'44 and arrived Milne Bay 17 Apr'44.
rows.note: Construction had stopped on 7 Jan 1944 to prepare to leave Woodlark.

rows.station: From 20th USN Construction Battalion, 2nd Section c/o FPO, San Francisco, Calif.
rows.note: The Second Section's roll for the quarter ending 31 Mar 1944, forwarded 17 Apr 1944. The card's reports for 1 Mar, 1 Apr and 1 May 1944: "operating at ABCD Annex, Russell Is." (ncbhist-020/p3).

rows.station: arrived Milne Bay 17 Apr'44. Departed Milne Bay 24 Apr'44
arrived at Brisbane 30 Apr'44. At present time quartered at Camp SeaBee near Brisbane
this Section embarked and departed from Brisbane on 2 Jun
1st and 2nd Sections of 20th CB reunited 6 Jun'44 at Russells
rows.note: "In June 1944, the first section of the 20th Battalion also arrived" (bases-25). The battalion's June and August reports name the Russells (Navy 60); a man who died on 12 Aug 1944 was buried in Banika Cemetery No. 11 (p0515).

rows.station: Tran. 28 Aug 1944 To Naval Advanced Base, Russells
rows.note: The August 1944 Report of Changes: the last transfers in the Russells are dated 21-28 Aug 1944, to the Receiving Ship, Navy 60, the Naval Advanced Base and Fleet Hospital No. 110 (p0512-p0516). The crossing home isn't dated.

rows.station: Battalion left Banika, Russell Islands for United States; 26 Officers, 997 Enlisted Men. One stop enroute at Guadalcanal.
rows.note: The ship isn't named.

rows.station: Arrived San Francisco, California, stationed at Camp Parks.
rows.note: The card: "20th CB arrived Parks from overseas via S.F. 30 Sep'44 with 27 off. and 997 men" (ncbhist-020/p4). The September roll's forwarding sheet: "Battalion has been on travel and leave status since 15 September 1944" (p0504).

rows.station: VCB TRAN NCTC DAVISVILLE R I 10 03 44
rows.note: Nearly the whole battalion transferred to the Naval Construction Training Center, Davisville, R.I., for leave, by train across the country. The date is the transfer's on the Camp Parks report; when the men reached Davisville, or went home on leave from it, isn't recorded.

rows.station: VCB REC NCTC DAVISVILLE R I 11 20 44
rows.note: Received back from Davisville at Camp Parks (Camp Parks Construction Battalion Replacement Depot), near Shoemaker, Calif.

rows.station: 20th U.S.N. Construction Battalion Camp Parks, Calif.
rows.note: The heading of the 31 Dec 1944 roll.

rows.station: ABD - Parks ... Left ABD - 1 Feb'45
rows.note: The card's "2nd Embarkation": Location "Saipan" struck out, "Okinawa" written in. Men who stayed behind were transferred to the CB Replacement Depot, Camp Parks, on 1 Feb 1945 (pp0697-0698). Where the battalion sailed from isn't given.

rows.station: To USNAB Dispensary, Navy 3237.
rows.note: A man left at the naval advance base dispensary, Eniwetok (Navy 3237), on 26 Feb 1945: the battalion was crossing the Pacific. On 10 Feb another went to the hospital at Navy 10 (Aiea, Oahu), but transfers there go on from Okinawa into July (evacuations), so they don't place the battalion.

rows.station: Arrived Saipan, Marianna Islands. 27 Officers, 1042 Enlisted Men.
rows.note: The card: "From the 1st to the 4th of Mar'45 the 20th CB was in transit & from the 5th to the 31st of Mar'45 staging on Saipan." The ship isn't named. On Saipan the battalion put up a building for an Army Coca-Cola plant (ncbhist-020/p9).

rows.station: To USN Base Hosp. Navy #3245.
rows.note: The April 1945 report sends men to and from the base hospital on Saipan (Navy 3245) from 9 to 26 April: the battalion was staging on Saipan. When it arrived isn't recorded (the March reports name no place).

rows.station: Upon orders from Port Director, Saipan, dated 11 April 1945, underway to Okinawa, Nansei Islands.
rows.note: The first echelon (23 officers, 749 men) "sailed from Saipan on four Land Ship Tanks" (ncbhist-020/p12); two are named in their war diaries: LST-898 loaded 250 men and 8 officers of the 20th at Pier C-4 on 9 April, and LST-824 210 men and 6 officers at dock C-4, Tanapag Harbor, on 8 April. See voyages.csv.

links.label: USS LST-898 war diary, 2/1/45 to 5/31/45, page 4

rows.station: At 1350 convoy was anchored in formation in Chimu Wan Bay ... this convoy was the first to enter the bay
rows.note: LST-898 beached at the western end of Chimu Wan on 19 April and disembarked its Seabees that day; LST-824 "finished unloading equipment and CBs passengers" at 1336 on 20 April (rg38-633416845/p0003).

links.label: USS LST-898 war diary, 2/1/45 to 5/31/45, page 5

rows.station: Trans. 3 May 45 Marine Corps Evacuation Hosp. No. 3 for treatment.
rows.note: Handwritten on the May 1945 report: the battalion was on Okinawa by 3 May. Men still came back from the Saipan hospital through May. Drawn at the camp near Chimu (below).

rows.station: Second Echelon of Four Officers and 277 Enlisted Men sailed from Saipan for Okinawa.
rows.note: The card has 276 men. The ship isn't named.

rows.station: Second Echelon arrived Okinawa. Battalion united.
rows.note: Drawn at the bivouac "near Gusikawa" that the 1 Jul 1945 report says the battalion left on 29 June (ncbhist-020/p5).

rows.station: During May, the 14th, 20th, and 40th Battalion camps near Chimu were attacked with light mortar and small-arms fire
rows.note: Okinawa's east coast, on Chimu Wan (Kin Bay). The card puts the battalion's bivouac near Gushikawa, on the bay's southern shore. Day of the month assumed. From June the sick go to the U.S.N. Operating Base and the Special Augmented Hospitals on Okinawa (Navy 3256) and to fleet hospitals; two men who died in June were buried in the 6th Marine Division's cemetery (p0745), and one who died on 17 July in the Island Command Cemetery, Okinawa (p0801).

rows.station: On 29 June, the batt moved from its bivouac area near Gusikawa into a permanent area about a mile from the Awashi Airstrip.
rows.note: The 1 Jul 1945 report. Drawn at Awase; the airstrip (Awase airfield) was being built by the Seabees (bases-30). On Okinawa the 20th also built waterfront facilities and worked at an advanced base construction depot on Ketchin Hento (ncbhist-020/p9).

rows.station: Tran., 29 Aug. 1945, To 79th USN Constr. Batt.
rows.note: The battalion broken up: the same page transfers its men to the 15th, 36th, 79th and 126th Battalions and to Commander Construction Troops, APO 331. Drawn at its camp near Awase. The battalion was inactivated on 8 November 1945 (ncbhist-020/p5).

rows.station: The 79th CB left U.S. 31 Jan'45 with 27 officers and 1060 men.
rows.note: From Camp Parks; CAPE BON departed 2 Feb 1945 with the battalion, routed via Pearl Harbor and Saipan (code names FRAY and HODE).

rows.station: Batt departed States 31 Jan'45 and arrived Saipan Staging Area on 26 Feb'45.
rows.note: The 1 Apr 1945 report.

rows.station: A, C, D Cos plus part of Hdqtrs Co, comprising 727 men and 21 off., left Saipan 18 April and arrived Okinawa 30 April.
rows.note: The 1 Jun 1945 report. B Company and the rest of headquarters (318 men) left Saipan on 7 May and arrived on 15 May. The 79th landed with the 11th Construction Brigade (bases-30). Where on Okinawa its camp was isn't given: drawn at the middle of the island.

rows.station: Received from 20th USNCB this date
rows.note: The Report of Changes for the month ending 1 Oct 1945: men received from the 20th Battalion on 2 Sep 1945. The card's reports for 1 Jul and 1 Aug 1945: "located at Okinawa" (ncbhist-079/p3).

rows.station: From 79th USNCB Navy 3256, c/o FPO, San Francisco, Calif.
rows.note: The forwarding sheet of the roll for the quarter ending 1 Oct 1945, forwarded 12 Oct 1945. Navy 3256 is Okinawa. From late September the battalion sends men home for discharge.

parts.note: The half that sailed from Port Hueneme on 6 Oct 1942 (the rolls' "Sec 2"); reunited with the second wave at Nouméa on 13 Dec 1942 (ncbhist-020/p2).
The half that stayed at Port Hueneme until 26 Nov 1942 (the rolls' "Section 1") (ncbhist-020/p2).
About 500 men: Townsville, Woodlark, Kiriwina, Milne Bay, Brisbane; the 1st Section from October 1943 (ncbhist-020/p2-p3).
The rest: Guadalcanal, the Russells, New Georgia, then Banika; the 2nd Section, its rolls headed "Detachment" and "Second Section" (ncbhist-020/p2-p3).

About 400 men (12 officers, 403 men; 1 1/2 companies) under Lt. Riordan at Oloana Bay, Vangunu (ncbhist-020/p2, p11; mcsol ch. 2). Its first echelon (3 officers, 114 men) left for Bau Island on 9 September 1943, its second (10 officers, 262 men) for Ondonga on 9 and 15 October (ncbhist-020/p11-p12).

About 140 men (3 officers, 142 men; one company) under Lt. Sanders at Viru Harbor (ncbhist-020/p2, p11); left in echelons on 5-9 September 1943 for East Rovianna and Doke Doke, and from East Rovianna for Bau Island, arriving 5 November (ncbhist-020/p11-p12).

The PT-boat base on Bau Island, Rendova Harbor: Group One's first echelon from 10 September 1943, joined by the Viru company on 5 November; 4 officers and 211 men left for the Russells on 9 January 1944 (ncbhist-020/p11-p12).
23 officers and 749 men, Saipan to Okinawa in four LSTs, 12-17 April 1945 (ncbhist-020/p12; LST-824 and LST-898 war diaries).
4 officers and 276-277 men, on Saipan until 7 May 1945; joined the first echelon on Okinawa on 14 May (ncbhist-020/p12, p5).

voyages.note: "Left United States, San Francisco, California." The narrative history has the arrival on 14 October; the chronology 20 October; Building the Navy's Bases 21 October (bases-24). No record found names the ship. A candidate, by its dates (inferred; no record of the battalion names her): the U.S. Army Transport President Coolidge sailed from San Francisco about 1100 on 6 Oct 1942 and "reached Noumea on the morning of October 20th, and discharged some navy personnel and their cargo", sailing on the afternoon of 24 Oct for Espiritu Santo, where she sank on mines on 26 Oct (the 172nd Infantry's history, NAID 404300670 p368: a destroyer and a dirigible "for the first half day; for the remainder of the voyage the transport was unescorted"). An officer aboard: she "had discharged approximately 1500 CBs with their gear and equipment at Noumea" (Espiritu Santo command history, NAID 77638874 p15), more than the first wave's 591 men, so she probably carried other Seabee units too.
"Left united States, Port Hueneme, California. (San Pedro, California)." The card dates the second wave's departure 26 November (ncbhist-020/p2). No record found names the ship.

voyages.ships: LST-334, LST-390, LST-446, LST-447, LST-448, LST-449; escorts SANDS and HUMPHREYS (Task Unit 32.6.2)
voyages.carried: "Acorn FIVE; Naval Base Unit; and, one half of the 20th Naval Construction Battalion"
voyages.note: Commander Amphibious Force, South Pacific's war diary: departed Nouméa 1600 local on 14 May 1943, arrived Townsville 0800 local on 20 May. Which half of the 20th went in which LST isn't recorded.

voyages.ships: McCAWLEY and PRESIDENT ADAMS, of Transport Division Two (Task Unit 32.8.2: PRESIDENT JACKSON, PRESIDENT HAYES, PRESIDENT ADAMS, McCAWLEY, LA SALLE), with six destroyers
voyages.carried: McCAWLEY: 70th Coast Artillery Unit, Naval Base personnel unit, 20th Naval Construction Battalion. PRESIDENT ADAMS: Naval Base personnel unit, 20th Naval Construction Battalion and 429th Signal Construction Company.
voyages.note: Transport Division Two's war diary logs the flagship's position at 0800, 1200 and 2000 each day (voyage_positions.csv). Japanese air raids were expected on 10 June; the destroyers' report of the action that evening is in an annex. Which of the two ships a man was in isn't recorded.

positions.fix_note: As typed this is 270 miles south-west of Nouméa 15 hours out, and 330 miles from the noon position; probably a slip, but the right figure can't be told. Left off the track.
As typed, 19° S is 600 miles south of the convoy's course; at 0800 it was sighting Rura Sura and Nugu Islands off Guadalcanal and anchored off Koli Point two hours later, so 9° 21' S.

voyages.carried: LST 354 - 800 tons of equipment for 20th Construction Battalion to North Renard, RUSSELL I.; LCT 62 and 133 - 150 tons each
voyages.note: Commander Task Group 32.3's war diary (cargo delivered 12 June 1943). The craft that carried the men aren't named.

voyages.ships: Seven LCIs (serials 1A-1G) and an LCT (serial 1N); with APDs WARD and SCHLEY carrying the Marine raiders
voyages.carried: LCIs: 20th C.B., 3 officers, 100 men, hand tools and demolition equipment to prepare the beaches for the LCTs. LCT 1N: 20th C.B. (less 1/2 Co), 3 officers, 128 men and 1,345 sq. ft. of vehicles
voyages.note: The Eastern Force loading order of 16 June 1943: loaded at Wernham Cove and the north side of Renard Sound on D-1 day (29 June), landed at Oleana Bay on D-day (30 June), Rear Admiral Fort commanding. A plan, not a record of what sailed; Rentz has the convoy off Oloana Bay at 0335 on 30 June (mcsol). Next day LCT 367 delivered 1 officer, 60 men and the 20th's vehicles and LCT 481 40 men and 161 tons (rg38-78141899/p0007).

voyages.ships: An LCI (serial 1U) and an LCT (serial 2J); the first echelon in APDs HOPKINS, ZANE, KILTY and CROSBY
voyages.carried: LCI 1U: Det Co "D", 20th C.B., 1 officer, 50 men, hand tools and demolition equipment. LCT 2J: 1/2 Co "D", 20th C.B., 3 officers, 62 men and 1,240 sq. ft. of vehicles
voyages.note: The loading order: the LCI to land at Viru on D-day, the LCT on D plus 1. The landing at Viru was delayed: Building the Navy's Bases has the first echelon land on 2 July (bases-25).

voyages.ships: LCT-145 and LCT-146, escorted by APc 37 and APc 42
voyages.carried: "one-half company of 20th Construction Battalion" (Oliana to MUNDA); 3 officers, 114 men (ncbhist-020/p11)
voyages.note: Commander Task Group 31.3's war diary of 8 September 1943 orders the two LCTs, loading at Oliana, to Munda; his monthly summary lists "20th Construction Battalion (1/2 company) Wickham to MUNDA", 125 men and 200 tons. The chronology has them leave Vangunu on 9 September and reach Bau Island on 10 September.

voyages.ships: APc 45 and LCT 367; LCTs returning from Torokina
voyages.note: Commander Task Group 31.3's war diary, 28 and 30 December 1943: APc 45 and LCT 367 on their way to Ondonga to load the 20th; the returning Torokina LCTs to complete the move from Ondonga to the Russells about 7 January. The Bau Island group (4 officers, 211 men) sailed on 9 January in craft not named.
One stop at Guadalcanal. No record found names the ship.
A man was left at the dispensary at Eniwetok on 26 February (rg24-190273312/p0698). No record found names the ship.

voyages.ships: Four LSTs (ncbhist-020/p12), two of them LST-824 and LST-898; convoy of LST Group 67 (flagship LST-802): 8-9 LSTs, 6 LSMs and 6 LCS(L)s with 4 destroyer escorts
voyages.carried: LST-824: 210 enlisted men and 6 officers, and CB equipment of the 20th NCB. LST-898: 250 men with gear and 8 officers of the 20th USN Construction Battalion
voyages.note: LST-824's war diary logs its position at 0800, 1200 and 2000 each day (voyage_positions.csv); it had loaded pontoon barges at Guam. The convoy was the first into Chimu Wan; LST-898 beached at its western end on 19 April and disembarked the Seabees; LST-824 finished unloading its "CBs passengers" on 20 April. The other two LSTs aren't named. The group flagship LST-802 moored at Saipan on 11 April "to load 20th, 40th and 42nd Naval Construction Battalions and their gear" (rg38-139998662/p0002) and on 18 April "Beached on Gushikawa Beach, Chimu Wan, Okinawa", completing the discharge of "cargo and seabees": probably the third of the four LSTs (inferred; it carried other battalions too). The convoy saw no attack: AA practice on 13 April, the flag lowered for Roosevelt the same day, a submarine contact depth-charged by an escort on 15 April, and air-raid alerts each night 17-20 April at Chimu Wan.
